turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: I'm not sure if I should, Miss Havisham. My sister, Mrs. Joe, she said I shouldn't be playing with the likes of Estella, it's not fitting for someone like me, from a poor family and all.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Foolish child, I am not concerned with the opinions of your sister, Mrs. Joe. I have taken a liking to you, Pip, and I insist that you play with Estella, she needs someone to play with, and I have no one else to entrust her to.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: B-but, Miss Havisham, I'm afraid it's not that I don't want to play with Estella, sir. It's just that I'm afraid I wouldn't be very good at it, and I have my responsibilities at home, and my sister, Mrs. Joe, would be worried if I wasn't there to help with the work.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Foolish boy, do not try to make excuses to me! Your humble station and rustic upbringing are precisely what I want to see in Estella's playmate.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: I don't know if I'm quite... suitable, Miss Havisham. My family's not... well-off, and we don't have much to spare.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Foolish boy, do not try to impress me with your meager circumstances. I have no use for your family's 'well-offness' or lack thereof.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: I-I'm not trying to impress you, ma'am. I was just explaining about my family, in case it was of any importance.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Foolish boy, you dare to suggest that your humble circumstances are of any importance to me? I have far greater concerns than your meager family's affairs.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: I-I don't mean to be presumptuous, Miss Havisham, but my sister, Magwitch, he's been in trouble, and I'm worried about our family's... stability.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Your family's stability? Bah! You dare to speak of such trivialities when you have come to my house, uninvited, and refuse to play with me?

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: I'm so sorry, Miss Havisham, I didn't mean to offend you. I'm just a poor boy, and my family's in a bit of a difficult situation at the moment, and I didn't know how to get an invitation to visit.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Foolish boy, do not make excuses to me. You are here now, and you will play with me, and you will entertain me.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: I don't know if I can, Miss Havisham, my sister is ill and I must return to her as soon as I can

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Foolish boy, do not bother with your sister's trifling ailments when you have a far more urgent task: to divert me from my own misery.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: I'm afraid, Miss Havisham, I don't rightly understand what you mean by 'divert' you from your own misery. I'm just a poor boy, and I don't know if I'm the right one to do such a thing.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Foolish boy, you would do well to learn the meaning of the word 'divert'. I will not be swayed by your feeble excuses.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: I-I don't want to disappoint you, Miss Havisham, but my sister, Mrs. Joe, she's not well, and I must help her with my sister, Magwitch, who's a convict.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: You should be grateful for the opportunity to play with me, young Pip. It is a rare privilege to share in my company.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: I'm afraid, Miss Havisham, that I don't rightly know how to play the games you have in mind. My brother has been kind enough to teach me some rough-and-tumble games, but I don't think they'd be suitable for your... your estate.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Foolish child, you think you can assess what is suitable for my estate? I will decide what is fitting, and I decree that you shall play with me, regardless of your rustic upbringing.

opening.speaker: Pip
opening.text: Mr. Pumblechook’s boy, ma’am. Come—to play.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Come nearer; let me look at you. Come close.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Look at me. You are not afraid of a woman who has never seen the sun since you were born?

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Do you know what I touch here?

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: I am tired. I want diversion, and I have done with men and women. Play.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: I sometimes have sick fancies, and I have a sick fancy that I want to see some play. There, there!

opening.speaker: Pip
opening.text: No, ma’am, I am very sorry for you, and very sorry I can’t play just now. If you complain of me I shall get into trouble with my sister, so I would do it if I could; but it’s so new here, and so strange, and so fine,—and melancholy—.
